package_info.package_versions: CLI built between July 3, 2018 and January 2024 (see below for variant-specific ranges)
package_info.why_malicious: The AWS Amplify CLI (and Amplify Studio) introduced a vulnerability in the IAM role trust policy templates it generated for Amplify projects. In certain versions, these templates created or modified IAM roles with trust policies that allowed any AWS account in the world to assume those roles via Cognito, without proper restrictions. This exposed privileged roles to global takeover, enabling attackers to gain access to AWS resources with the permissions of those roles. The vulnerability persisted for years, affecting a large number of projects and roles.

execution_context.trigger: infrastructure provisioning (project creation or auth removal)
execution_context.file_location: CloudFormation template / IAM role trust policy (generated by Amplify CLI or Studio)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During project creation or when removing the authentication component, the code sets the IAM role trust policy to allow any principal federated via cognito-identity.amazonaws.com to assume the role using sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, with no conditions restricting the identity pool, enabling global role assumption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This trust policy allows any Cognito identity pool in any AWS account to assume the role, with no restrictions. This is equivalent to making the role globally assumable.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, IAM trust policies for Cognito roles should restrict assumption to a specific identity pool (via a Condition on cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud) and user type (authenticated/unauthenticated). The actual policy omits these restrictions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A trust policy might be temporarily open for testing in a non-production environment, but should never be used in production or for privileged roles.
key_indicators: No Condition element restricting audience or authentication method

execution_context.trigger: infrastructure provisioning (project creation, default for CLI July 2018–Aug 2019)
execution_context.file_location: CloudFormation template / IAM role trust policy (generated by Amplify CLI)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During project creation (CLI July 2018–Aug 2019), the code sets the IAM role trust policy to allow any principal federated via cognito-identity.amazonaws.com to assume the role using sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, with a condition only on the authentication method (amr), but not restricting the identity pool, enabling global role assumption by any authenticated Cognito user.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This trust policy allows any authenticated Cognito user from any identity pool in any AWS account to assume the role, as there is no restriction on the audience (identity pool).
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A secure trust policy should restrict both the authentication method and the specific identity pool (audience). This policy only restricts the authentication method, not the pool.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A developer might intend to allow all authenticated users in a single pool, but not globally.

execution_context.trigger: infrastructure provisioning (project creation, default for CLI July 2018–Aug 2019)
execution_context.file_location: CloudFormation template / IAM role trust policy (generated by Amplify CLI)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During project creation (CLI July 2018–Aug 2019), the code sets the IAM role trust policy to allow any unauthenticated Cognito user from any identity pool in any AWS account to assume the role using sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, with no restriction on the identity pool.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This trust policy allows any unauthenticated Cognito user from any identity pool in any AWS account to assume the role, as there is no restriction on the audience (identity pool).
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A secure trust policy should restrict both the authentication method and the specific identity pool (audience). This policy only restricts the authentication method, not the pool.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A developer might intend to allow all unauthenticated users in a single pool, but not globally.

execution_context.file_location: Python script for auditing IAM roles (provided in the article)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script enumerates all IAM roles and checks their trust policies for the absence of a Condition restricting the audience (cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud), flagging roles that are globally assumable via Cognito.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This script is not malicious, but is included as a detection mechanism for the above vulnerabilities. It programmatically identifies roles with overly permissive trust policies.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal IAM audit scripts should check for least-privilege and proper trust policy conditions. This script specifically looks for the absence of such conditions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use for security auditing and compliance.
key_indicators: Checks for missing or empty Condition in trust policy
Flags roles with Principal cognito-identity.amazonaws.com and Action sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity

attack_chain.action: Amplify CLI or Studio creates or modifies IAM roles with overly permissive trust policies (variant one or two).
attack_chain.leads_to: IAM roles are globally assumable via Cognito.

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers the ARN of a vulnerable role (e.g., via public code, deterministic naming, or web scraping).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is able to target a specific role for assumption.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a Cognito identity pool in their own AWS account and generates a web identity token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is able to use the token to attempt role assumption.

attack_chain.action: Attacker calls sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with the vulnerable role's ARN and their web identity token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives STS credentials for the victim role.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the assumed role's credentials to access AWS resources with the permissions of the compromised role.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves privilege escalation or data access in the victim AWS account.

behavioral_signatures: IAM role trust policy with Principal.Federated = cognito-identity.amazonaws.com and Action = sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, but missing Condition on cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud
CloudTrail events for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity where the identityProvider is cognito-identity.amazonaws.com and the audience (identity pool) is not owned by the account
IAM roles with names ending in authRole or unauthRole and no audience restriction in trust policy
file_indicators: IAM role trust policies lacking Condition on cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud
CloudFormation templates generated by Amplify CLI/Studio with permissive trust policies
network_indicators: Unusual sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API calls from external identity pools
CloudTrail logs with userIdentity.identityProvider = cognito-identity.amazonaws.com and responseElements.audience not matching known pools
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Enumerate all IAM roles in your AWS account and inspect their trust policies. Flag any role with Principal.Federated = cognito-identity.amazonaws.com and Action = sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity that does not include a Condition restricting cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud to a specific identity pool. Monitor CloudTrail for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events where the audience (identity pool) is not owned by your account, as this may indicate attempted exploitation. Pay special attention to roles with names ending in authRole or unauthRole, as these are commonly affected.
